newsitem.title: CANADA: Ivaco sees Canron deal, profitable 1997.
newsitem.headline: Ivaco sees Canron deal, profitable 1997.

text.p: Ivaco Inc said on Thursday it was in the final stage of negotiations to sell its Canron structural steel fabrication business.
Ivaco told the annual meeting that the deal was expected to close in the third quarter and generate about C$35 million to C$40 million in cash, including the realization of working capital.
Ivaco Chief Executive Paul Ivanier said he expected 1997 to be profitable for Ivaco and that earnings would be probably be "substantially higher" in 1998 than in 1997.
"We expect a good and profitable year for Ivaco in 1997," Ivanier said in a statement.
"We also believe that if the world unfolds as we believe it will, it is probable that Ivaco will post earnings substantially higher in 1998 than those of 1997," he added.

In April Ivaco reported first-quarter net earnings of C$5.4 million, or C$0.05 per share, compared to a loss of C$2.7 million or C$0.38 per share in the same period of last year. The 1996 results included a loss from dicontinued operations of C$4.2 million from the divestiture of Atlantic Steel operations.
Ivanier said in a statement that the sale of Canron will represent the final step in Ivaco's program to exit non-core businesses.

In his review of the company's activities, Ivanier reported that in the 1996 fiscal year Ivaco had divested four non-core businesses. The four were sold for C$184 million, of which C$156 million was received in cash.
Ivaco announced earlier this month that its Atlantic Steel subsidiary has signed an agreement to sell its property in mid-town Atlanta for cash proceeds of US$76 million (Cdn $105 million).

Atlantic will be responsible for environmental remediation. The property is carried on Atlantic's books at its original cost of US$800 thousand. Ivaco said taxes on the gain will be largely offset by unused tax losses. Closing is expected during 1999.

Ivaco reiterated that it will invest significantly in the remaining core businesses including a C$90 million investment in quality enhancement and expansions of which about one-half is at Ivaco Rolling Mills and the balance is at Ifastgroupe, the Sivaco Wire Group and IPEX.

"The strength in Ivaco's productivity and its penetration into the desired new value-added products that will result from these initiatives will prove that Ivaco has taken the right road. It will prove that short-term pain for long-term gain was the right road," Ivanier said.
